cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: PLEASE READ AT LEAST 1500 LINES AT A TIME DONT DO PARTIAL READS
cards.claim: His global rule forces whole-file reads (minimum 1500 lines) because partial reads make the model add duplicate functions that already exist deeper in the file.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as a rule with a failure story, no numbers.
cards.landing: A short always-loaded read-whole-file rule in CLAUDE.md or the explorer agent prompt; counters the repo's habit of limit/offset reads.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: DELETE 10% minimum from every file you touch
cards.claim: He mandates deleting at least 10% of every touched file and 'ALWAYS REDUCE AND DELETE AS MUCH CODE AS POSSIBLE' as a standing agent rule.
cards.evidence_detail: Imperative rule, no measurement; also appears as a verification checklist item.
cards.landing: A deletion-bias line in a phase checklist or reviewer prompt; conflicts with FixFlow's money/ledger code where deletion is risky.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Each file change should include a test change or new test
cards.claim: Rule that every changed file is paired with a test change, plus run linters immediately and run tests after each change.
cards.evidence_detail: One line in a rules list.
cards.landing: A reviewer check that each changed source file has a matching test diff, citable per register id.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Change as few files at a time as possible
cards.claim: Rule to keep each change touching as few files as possible.
cards.evidence_detail: One line, no rationale given.
cards.landing: A per-phase diff-size guard in the ship-plan routine or reviewer prompt.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Adopt the persona of legendary Programmer Uncle Bob
cards.claim: The file opens with a persona line and ends with flattering 'you are different from other models' framing ('Other models partial-read... You're different') to motivate compliance.
cards.evidence_detail: Persona/motivational prompting, no test.
cards.landing: Not obviously adoptable; a data point on his personal CLAUDE.md style versus his published 'short, universally applicable' guidance (Kyle/Dex blog posts).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Once you've done the 1500-line read, YOU HAVE COMPLETE CONTEXT. Don't second-guess yourself.
cards.claim: After a full read the agent is told not to re-read or second-guess, trading verification for forward momentum.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule; tension with refute-by-default reviewing.
cards.landing: A counter-example for the harness: his personal config trusts the implementer, while FixFlow's reviewers assume refutation.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If a git operation fails like a `git push` stop immediately and tell me what happened
cards.claim: On any failed git operation (his yubikey push) the agent must stop and report rather than retry or work around it.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule with a concrete human-in-the-loop reason (physical key touch).
cards.landing: A stop-and-report rule for failed push/deploy steps in the phase routine, matching the repo's deploy-trap list.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: After creating a worktree, you MUST run `make -C WORKTREE_DIR setup` to install deps etc
cards.claim: Worktree creation is a fixed checklist: copy settings.local.json and .env, run make setup, run make thoughts, then launch the implementer with the single /implement_plan command.
cards.evidence_detail: Five MUST steps in the file.
cards.landing: A saved worktree-bootstrap script or skill; the repo's session-per-phase routine could script these steps instead of prose.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use `codelayer launch --model opus -w WORKTREE_PATH "/implement_plan"` (not cd + launch
cards.claim: New sessions are launched via CLI with an explicit worktree path, always the opus model, and only the single /implement_plan command, so the handoff is a file and the fresh session starts clean.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule in the 'Launching new sessions' section.
cards.landing: Matches the one-phase-per-new-session defence; the pattern is 'launch carries one command, state lives in a file'.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: AFTER FETCHING THE TICKET - PAUSE and ask the user how you want to proceed.
cards.claim: A fetch step (Linear ticket into thoughts/shared/tickets) is followed by a mandatory pause with a scripted menu (research, plan, or other) rather than auto-proceeding.
cards.evidence_detail: Scripted response template.
cards.landing: An explicit checkpoint at phase entry in the routine: ingest, then ask which mode.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If you are writing a one-off script for python, you must use uv scripts
cards.claim: One-off Python scripts must be self-contained uv scripts with dependencies declared in a header comment, so they run with no environment setup.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule with template; note CLAUDE.md here says no python on PATH in the user's setup is a separate concern.
cards.landing: A convention for saved verifier/audit scripts (self-describing, dependency-declared) in a workflow library.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: ENV files (.env/.env.local) contain secrets - NEVER modify them
cards.claim: Hard rule that env files are never modified by the agent.
cards.evidence_detail: One line; no enforcement mechanism (no hook or deny rule in settings.json).
cards.landing: Prose-only guard; the contrast with a settings deny rule is the point (his settings.json has no deny list).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: use Linear branch names when available (from gitBranchName field)
cards.claim: Branch and worktree names derive from the ticket system field; if only a number is known, infer the team prefix from branch name or $PWD.
cards.evidence_detail: Naming rule.
cards.landing: A branch-naming rule tying each phase PR to its plan register id.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: "MAX_THINKING_TOKENS": "32000"
cards.claim: His personal setup sets a 32000 thinking-token budget, while the claudelayer project config sets only 4000 with alwaysThinkingEnabled false.
cards.evidence_detail: Two config values in two repos; no stated reason or comparison.
cards.landing: A thinking-budget knob per agent/role (verifiers vs explorers); his own repos differ by 8x.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "model": "opus"
cards.claim: The project pins the default model to opus and keeps thinking low (4000 tokens, alwaysThinkingEnabled false), with per-agent model overrides for sonnet in agent files.
cards.evidence_detail: Config file; commands research_codebase/create_plan/iterate_plan set model: opus, exhaustive-research sets sonnet, implement_plan sets none.
cards.landing: Role-based model routing in command frontmatter (planning and research on opus; fan-out on sonnet; locator on inherit).

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_WORKING_DIR": "1"
cards.claim: The config sets bash to maintain its working directory, auto-allows only the spec_metadata script, and raises MCP_TIMEOUT to 1000000.
cards.evidence_detail: Config values only; the allow-list is a single script, so metadata gathering is the only pre-approved shell action.
cards.landing: Pre-approve only the metadata script a routine needs; a metadata script (commit sha, branch, date) as the single trusted source for document frontmatter.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: model: sonnet
cards.claim: The 'recursive' analyzer is the plain analyzer prompt with only the model pinned to sonnet and tools Read, Grep, Glob, LS; the recursion is not in the prompt but in how it is launched.
cards.evidence_detail: Diffed by reading: prompt body is identical to dotfiles codebase-analyzer (which uses model: inherit).
cards.landing: Agent files can pin a cheaper model for fan-out analysis while the parent runs opus; the explorer is Haiku today.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: if `your_number` is < 10, run `mcp__agent-launch` and tell it a new number
cards.claim: Sub-agent recursion is a toy proof: an agent gets a number, launches a copy of itself through an MCP agent-launch tool with number+1 until 10, then each level writes outputs/N.md and reports the path, bypassing the built-in no-nesting limit.
cards.evidence_detail: Demo agent with a 10-level stop condition; no performance data.
cards.landing: Recursion via a launcher MCP tool with an explicit depth counter and file outputs as the return channel, a way to nest sub-agents beyond one level.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: use the `Task` tool IN PARALLEL to launch a general-purpose agent with the directory name
cards.claim: A fan-out command lists top-level directories, launches one general-purpose agent per directory in parallel, each of which in turn uses the agent-launch MCP to start locator+analyzer and then analyzer+pattern agents, and the top level merges into one markdown summary.
cards.evidence_detail: Seven-line command; no results or cost reported.
cards.landing: A saved workflow template: per-slice recursive explore then one synthesis, which suits FixFlow's slice layout (identity, jobs, media...).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: YOUR ONLY JOB IS TO DOCUMENT AND EXPLAIN THE CODEBASE AS IT EXISTS TODAY
cards.claim: The research command forbids suggestions, root-cause analysis, critique and recommendations from the main agent and every sub-agent, so research output is a neutral map and not an opinion.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated across the command and all three codebase agents; the later 'Everything We Got Wrong About RPI' material attributes failures to research prompts returning opinions.
cards.landing: Research prompts in the phase routine: ask for what exists with file:line, keep judgement for the plan step.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Read these files yourself in the main context before spawning any sub-tasks
cards.claim: The main agent must read user-mentioned files fully (no limit/offset) before spawning sub-agents, then keep itself on synthesis, not deep file reading, and wait for ALL sub-agents before synthesizing.
cards.evidence_detail: Ordering rules ('Follow the numbered steps exactly').
cards.landing: A rule for the orchestrating session: read the directly named files itself, delegate wide search, never synthesize before all workers return.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Prioritize live codebase findings as primary source of truth
cards.claim: Live code outranks the thoughts/ store, which is only supplementary historical context, and research is always rerun fresh rather than trusting old research documents.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in steps 4 and the notes ('never rely solely on existing research documents').
cards.landing: A knowledge-store read rule: stored diagnoses are leads to re-verify against current code, matching the cold-resume trial.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Run the `hack/spec_metadata.sh` script to generate all relevant metadata
cards.claim: Every research document gets YAML frontmatter (date, researcher, git_commit, branch, repository, topic, tags, status, last_updated) produced by a script, with 'NEVER write the research document with placeholder values', and follow-ups append a dated section and update last_updated.
cards.evidence_detail: Template plus ordering rule (metadata before document).
cards.landing: The 'Plan @ <sha>' convention is the same idea; a metadata script gives auditable provenance for every journal and store entry.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't write detailed prompts about HOW to search - the agents already know
cards.claim: The orchestrator tells sub-agents what to look for, not how to search, and reminds them they are documenting; the locator is used first and analyzers only on the most promising findings.
cards.evidence_detail: Guidance bullets.
cards.landing: Short delegation prompts to the Haiku explorer; two-stage locate-then-analyze.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Add GitHub permalinks (if applicable)
cards.claim: Research output references use commit-pinned GitHub permalinks (owner/repo/blob/commit/file#Lline) when the commit is pushed, so citations survive later edits.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 7 of the command.
cards.landing: Commit-pinned citations in verified diagnoses, needed for the cold-resume trial to be checkable.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: DO NOT just accept the correction
cards.claim: When the human corrects the agent's understanding, the planner must spawn new research to verify the correction before proceeding, and must not accept it on authority.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 2 rule.
cards.landing: A verify-the-claim rule that applies to owner statements and to prior-session notes alike.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do NOT write the plan with unresolved questions
cards.claim: A plan may not be written with open questions; the planner must stop and research or ask, and the plan must include a 'What We're NOT Doing' section against scope creep.
cards.evidence_detail: Guideline 6 and template section.
cards.landing: A gate on the draft PR 'Plan @ sha': zero open questions, explicit out-of-scope list.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Always separate success criteria into two categories
cards.claim: Every plan phase splits success criteria into Automated Verification (runnable commands, e.g. make targets) and Manual Verification (human), and automated steps should use `make` targets where possible.
cards.evidence_detail: Template and guideline; the implementer may only tick manual boxes after the user confirms.
cards.landing: Two-bucket criteria per register id; automated bucket becomes the reviewer's checkable evidence (fail-before/pass-after).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't write the full plan in one shot
cards.claim: Planning is staged for human buy-in: present understanding and questions, then design options, then a phase outline for approval, and only then the detailed plan file, with the sync step after each edit.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 1-5; this is the interactive RPI planning loop that his 2026 talks later say needed splitting (an 85-instruction planning prompt, per the inventory).
cards.landing: Outline-before-detail checkpoint in the plan phase; evidence that the original plan command was one long prompt.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Be EXTREMELY specific about directories
cards.claim: Sub-task prompts must name exact directories, expected output format, read-only tools and file:line references, and the planner must verify unexpected sub-task results with follow-ups.
cards.evidence_detail: Sub-task Spawning Best Practices list (8 items).
cards.landing: A delegation-brief template for the explorer and workflow workers (scope path, tools, output shape, citation requirement).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If instructed to execute multiple phases consecutively, skip the pause until the last phase.
cards.claim: Default is one phase per run, with a mandatory pause after automated checks pass and a fixed 'Phase N Complete - Ready for Manual Verification' message; manual-check boxes are not ticked until the user confirms.
cards.evidence_detail: Identical text in command and agent file.
cards.landing: Basis for the six-question closing message; confirms one-phase-per-session as his default shape.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Trust that completed work is done
cards.claim: Resume rule: if the plan has checkmarks, trust them, start from the first unchecked item, and verify earlier work only if something seems off; progress lives as checkboxes in the plan file itself.
cards.evidence_detail: 'Resuming Work' section.
cards.landing: Resume-from-the-file state; note it trusts checkmarks, which cold-resume trial should test against repository evidence.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Present the issue clearly
cards.claim: On a plan/reality mismatch the implementer must STOP and present Expected / Found / Why this matters, then ask how to proceed; sub-tasks are used sparingly in implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Fixed mismatch template.
cards.landing: A structured deviation record in the decisions journal (Expected / Found / Why).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: model: sonnet
cards.claim: The implementer is a custom agent on Sonnet with Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash, TodoWrite, Task tools whose body is the implement_plan command, so one text serves as slash command and agent.
cards.evidence_detail: Frontmatter plus body identical to the command.
cards.landing: Turning a phase routine into an agent file with a pinned model and tool list rather than relying on session defaults.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring one of these tools more than once.
cards.claim: The locator has tools Grep, Glob, LS only (no Read), is told not to read file contents, and its description tells the parent to use it whenever it would run grep/glob more than once; model is inherit, not a small model.
cards.evidence_detail: Frontmatter and 'Don't read file contents' guideline.
cards.landing: Compare with FixFlow's Haiku locator: tool-restriction to enforce locate-only, and the delegation trigger written into the description.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Always include file:line references for claims
cards.claim: The analyzer returns a fixed format (Overview, Entry Points, Core Implementation, Data Flow, Key Patterns, Configuration, Error Handling) with file:line for every claim and 'Don't guess about implementation'.
cards.evidence_detail: Output-format spec; the model is inherit and the prompt says 'ultrathink'.
cards.landing: A fixed output schema with mandatory file:line for sub-agent returns, making claims checkable by a refuter.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: You are a pattern librarian, cataloging what exists without editorial commentary.
cards.claim: The pattern-finder returns concrete code snippets with file:line plus the existing test pattern for similar features, forbidding any ranking of patterns, which gives planners templates to model from.
cards.evidence_detail: Agent body; note the prompt contradicts itself ('Note which approach is preferred' vs 'Don't recommend').
cards.landing: A second custom agent beside the locator: 'find the closest existing slice implementation and its test' for new migrations/endpoints.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: You're a curator of insights, not a document summarizer.
cards.claim: Notes are read through two agents: a locator that only lists thoughts/ documents by type, and an analyzer that extracts decisions, constraints, specs and open items while filtering superseded or exploratory content and assessing relevance now.
cards.evidence_detail: Two agent prompts; analyzer output includes 'Status: still relevant/implemented/superseded'.
cards.landing: Design input for the knowledge-store reader: locate by type, then extract decisions with a staleness/relevance verdict.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Handle thoughts/searchable/ (read-only directory for searching)
cards.claim: The thoughts store has shared/, per-user, and global areas (tickets, research, plans, prs), with a hard-linked read-only searchable/ copy for grep and a path-correction rule that strips only 'searchable/' from reported paths.
cards.evidence_detail: Directory tree in the agent prompt.
cards.landing: A filesystem layout for the knowledge store (typed folders, dated filenames, searchable mirror) that agents can grep without new infrastructure.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Start with 2-3 well-crafted searches before fetching content
cards.claim: The web researcher is capped: 2-3 searches, fetch only the 3-5 best pages, quote exactly with links, and note dates and gaps; the research command only uses it if the user explicitly asks.
cards.evidence_detail: Search Efficiency section; web agents are opt-in in research_codebase.
cards.landing: Budgeted search limits and 'gaps' section in any research agent the harness adds.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The goal is to compact and summarize your context without losing any of the key details
cards.claim: Handoff is a command that writes a timestamped markdown file (thoughts/shared/handoffs/<ticket>/date_time_ticket_slug.md) with frontmatter and sections Task(s), Critical References (2-3 only), Recent changes (file:line), Learnings, Artifacts, Action Items, Other Notes, then syncs it.
cards.evidence_detail: Template; it is his hand-written form of intentional compaction.
cards.landing: A resume document template for the phase closing message or P1 cold-resume test: the ten frozen facts could map to these sections.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: avoid large code blocks or diffs; do not include one unless it's necessary
cards.claim: Handoffs should prefer path:line references over pasted code, include 'more information, not less', and list an exhaustive artifacts list for the next agent.
cards.evidence_detail: Additional Notes; the instruction is to be thorough yet concise, which pulls both ways.
cards.landing: Reference-not-copy rule for session handoffs so the next session reads sources rather than stale excerpts.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: come up with a prompt and session title for a new agent to pick up where you left off
cards.claim: A personal command has the agent write a continuation prompt and session title, show it to the user, and on approval launch a new opus session in the same directory via the humanlayer CLI.
cards.evidence_detail: 11-line command; includes a typo in the CLI name (humanalyer).
cards.landing: A 'continue in a new session' command: prompt + title, human approval, then launch; shorter than the full handoff file.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Can query directly with `sqlite3`
cards.claim: A session-forensics command reconstructs what past agent sessions did by querying the orchestrator's SQLite database (raw_events with result events in the last 24 hours), its logs and git state, then writes a report of research, plan and implement sessions.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes tooling for finding what was done where; no outcomes.
cards.landing: The audit-from-outside idea behind W2: independent session records (transcripts, final-result events) checked against claimed phase compliance.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If it passes, mark the checkbox as checked: `- [x]`
cards.claim: PR descriptions follow a repository template; the agent must run each runnable 'How to verify it' command, tick the box only on pass, leave failures unticked with the reason, and flag manual steps for the user.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 6; it also saves the description in thoughts/shared/prs and pushes it with gh pr edit --body-file.
cards.landing: PR body checkboxes that are only ticked by a command actually run in-session; evidence for the reviewer.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: read ./claude/commands/commit.md and create a commit, then read ./claude/commands/describe_pr.md and create a PR
cards.claim: One launch prompt chains the whole tail: implement the plan, commit, describe the PR, comment on the ticket; a worktree is created from a script, and the plan is referenced by a relative thoughts/ path that is synced across worktrees. The launch is shown to the human for confirmation first.
cards.evidence_detail: Command text; note the path ./claude/commands omits the dot as written.
cards.landing: A single saved launch prompt per phase (implement, commit, PR description, ticket comment) with a human confirmation of the exact command.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use `git add` with specific files (never use `-A` or `.`)
cards.claim: Commits are planned and shown to the user for approval, staged by explicit file only, and carry no Claude attribution or Co-Authored-By lines.
cards.evidence_detail: Commit command; the no-attribution rule differs from the attribution this harness's system reminder requests.
cards.landing: Explicit-file staging as a commit rule; his no-attribution stance conflicts with the current attribution instruction (flag for the owner).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: HUMAN_MESSAGE=$(echo "$CLAUDE_ANSWER" | npx humanlayer contact_human -m -)
cards.claim: A headless loop runs `claude -p`, sends each answer to a human via a contact_human channel, feeds the reply back with --continue and routes permission prompts through an MCP approvals tool (--permission-prompt-tool).
cards.evidence_detail: A 35-line shell prototype with an allowedTools variable; not production.
cards.landing: A human-approval channel for headless runs; shows approval can be an external tool, not a prompt in the terminal.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: model="claude-3-5-haiku-latest"
cards.claim: A tiny personal CLI streams a one-shot prompt to the small Haiku model with max_tokens 1024 for quick questions, i.e. cheap model on the command line as a default tool.
cards.evidence_detail: 22-line script on an old Haiku (3.5) alias; no stated use.
cards.landing: A cheap-model shell tool for classification or log-trimming steps that do not need the main agent.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: BLOCK=${expressions[$RANDOM % ${#expressions[@]}]}
cards.claim: cblock prints a random block glyph after a label, a prompt-decoration script with no bearing on harness behaviour.
cards.evidence_detail: 8-line script.
cards.landing: None.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: focused agents with specific workflows, rules, and expertise areas
cards.claim: multiclaude ships five role personas (developer, code-reviewer, rebaser, merger, multiplan-manager) as markdown files plus a staged CLAUDE.md to merge in, installed by `npx multiclaude init`, so roles are selected by telling the agent which persona file to adopt.
cards.evidence_detail: README only; persona files not read, no usage data; date not in the file.
cards.landing: Role persona files (reviewer, merger) as reusable library entries; each phase picks a persona rather than carrying all rules in CLAUDE.md.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: npx multiclaude launch branch-name plan-file.md
cards.claim: A manager persona splits a large feature into worker plans and uses a launch command (branch + plan file) and a cleanup command to run coding agents in parallel, relying on Makefile setup and teardown targets that init creates.
cards.evidence_detail: README description; no results.
cards.landing: A branch+plan-file launch contract as the unit of parallel work; Makefile setup/teardown as the worktree interface.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Commits every 5-10 minutes with meaningful progress
cards.claim: The developer persona keeps 20+ item TODO lists, commits every 5-10 minutes, and deletes more code than it adds; the rebaser squashes later into a clean history after making a backup branch, and the merger tests after each merge.
cards.evidence_detail: Bulleted persona summaries; rules are in unread persona files.
cards.landing: Frequent small commits plus a separate history-cleanup role; backup-branch-before-rebase as a rule.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Follows "read 1500+ lines first" rule to understand context
cards.claim: The 1500-line read rule from his global CLAUDE.md is reused in the developer and merger personas, so it is a shared convention across his tooling, not a one-off.
cards.evidence_detail: Appears twice in the README.
cards.landing: The same rule family as R44-1; shows he repeats rules across files, which cuts against a short CLAUDE.md.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: model: opus
cards.claim: Model is set per command: research_codebase, create_plan and iterate_plan are opus, exhaustive-research is sonnet, implement_plan has no model line, so planning/research get the strongest model and the fan-out gets the cheaper one.
cards.evidence_detail: Frontmatter read across commands; no cost or quality comparison.
cards.landing: Per-phase model routing in the ship plan (research/plan on a strong model, mechanical fan-out cheaper); no effort level is set, only model.

gaps: Repo date for multiclaude is not in the README; 2025-06~ is an estimate.
multiclaude persona files (agent-developer.md etc.) and CLAUDE.staged.md were not in my file list, so persona rules beyond the README summary are unread.
No resume_handoff command was in the bundle; create_handoff points to it but its text was not read.
No hooks directory or hooks config appears in either settings.json; the bundle shows no hook-based enforcement.
The claudelayer recursion mechanism depends on an mcp__agent-launch MCP server whose config was not in the bundle (no .mcp.json read).
hack/spec_metadata.sh and hack/create_worktree.sh referenced by the commands were not provided.

new_sources.title: dexhorthy/dotfiles (global ~/.claude config and .bin scripts)
new_sources.why: First-hand personal harness: global CLAUDE.md, seven agents, two commands, settings; not in inventory.

new_sources.title: humanlayer/multiclaude
new_sources.why: Persona CLI for developer/reviewer/rebaser/merger/manager roles; not in inventory.
